evidence:
Defining behaviour is graded. The product is a custom code editor plus Run-in-preview with saved revisions (instruction.md: 'paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source'). tests/scored/functional/judge.toml grades it directly with real input: cw_custom_typing_and_line_join (line 24), cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic (line 96), cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo (line 186) and cw_basic_run_output (line 213: 'type a one-line JavaScript program that adds two three-digit integers you choose ... Press Run: the preview must show the correct sum and the app console must contain it. Change one of the two integers ... Run again: the preview must show the new sum'). The second run with a judge-chosen changed operand excludes a canned preview.

State is proven durable and server-held. cw_save_reload_restart (judge.toml line 339): 'Save once, and note its library entry, its revision and its history. Then clear this origin's browser storage as described in the application notes and reload: the library must still show that record, and opening it must show the exact title, filename and source, as one record. Then call the verifier-provided restart_app tool once. After it reports a completed restart, a fresh page must show the same single record with the same revision, title, filename, source and history. Do not infer a restart from a reload or a health response.' app_context.md defines the clearing exhaustively ('clears localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB databases, Cache Storage, the origin private file system, service worker registrations and cookies for this origin, then reload'), so a browser-storage-only library fails the reload leg and a process-memory-only server fails the restart leg. The requirement is public: behaviour.md 'A fresh page must read the saved record from the running app, and saved work and history must survive a complete server restart'; integration.md 'Saved snippets, their record ids and revisions must survive page reloads and complete process restarts.' No account exists (app_context.md 'Accounts: None'), so the re-auth leg does not apply.

No same-origin demand. The server-backing proof is 'record survives clearing this origin's storage and a real process restart'; no criterion or prompt requires requests to stay same-origin, and app_context.md says 'Network access to public assets by the app itself is allowed and is not a failure.' The only fetch restriction graded (cw_preview_isolation) concerns user code in the preview and is a public requirement in security.md.

Tool feasibility. functional/judge.toml lines 14-18 wire the verifier MCP server to $APP_RESTART_HELPER; test.sh writes app-restart.sh, which kills the app process group and relaunches the same entry with the same DB_PATH; restart_mcp.py is single-use, and exactly one criterion calls it (prompt.md 'Only the criterion that names it may call the restart_app tool ... and only once'). Task test.sh and restart_mcp.py are identical to the frozen template. The golden keeps only pane sizes in localStorage (src/app.tsx lines 35-36, 108), so the storage clear cannot break it; server.js stores snippets, revisions and restore operations in SQLite at DB_PATH.

Measured evidence. On these bytes, scripted only: results/persist-before.json reports cw_shared_saved_record and cw_save_reload_restart(before) true, results/persist-after.json reports cw_save_reload_restart true after run_golden.sh replaced the node process (pkill then relaunch on the same DB_PATH); the after phase used a newly launched browser, so the re-read could not have come from browser storage. Hosted judge, earlier candidate only (QC input 4f93c627): cw_save_reload_restart value 1.0, reasoning quotes the tool reply 'restart complete: the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP' and a full storage clear. That criterion text has since changed (the marker must now be typed inside the first line), so no configured-judge observation exists for the current wording; this is the round-wide evidence gap already stated in the index, not a defect of this row.

Residual observation, P3, not a Fail: the criterion clears browser storage before the restart but not again after it, and the judge's 'fresh page' after the restart is in the same browser context. A contrived app with a memory-only server and a client that mirrors the library into localStorage and re-uploads it when the server comes back empty would refill its mirror on the post-clear reload and then pass the restart leg. I do not rate this as a credible failure: it needs deliberate re-seeding code, the brief mandates SQLite with better-sqlite3 supplied, and the clear-then-reload leg already proves the record is held by the server. Adding 'clear this origin's browser storage again before opening the fresh page' after the restart would close it at the cost of one script call.

Outside this row: the render gate was reduced to load-and-type and does not itself prove server backing (check 29 territory); server backing is carried by the scored criterion above.
